title: Optical and magnetic signatures of drive-enhanced coherence in phase-disordered superconducting bilayers
authors: Duilio De Santis, Sambuddha Chattopadhyay, Marios H. Michael, Andrea Cavalleri, Gil Refael, Patrick A. Lee, Eugene A. Demler
abstract: Recent experiments demonstrating superconducting-like characteristics in materials above their equilibrium transition temperatures following strong sub-picosecond optical excitation have stimulated theoretical interest in phase-disordered superconductors subject to a periodically modulated superfluid stiffness. Previous analyses of the single-layer optical conductivity have shown that such a drive can enhance the low-frequency $1/ω$ response, even when the period-averaged stiffness remains unchanged. We extend these studies to bilayer systems, such as the YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$ (YBCO) cuprate, by considering drives with different symmetries. Specifically, we investigate a layer-symmetric drive, in which the two planes stiffen and soften simultaneously, and a layer-antisymmetric drive, in which one plane stiffens while the other softens. Both drives enhance correlations of the layer-averaged phase and generate comparable superconducting-like optical conductivities. Only the symmetric drive, however, strengthens relative-phase locking and the associated counterflow response to a magnetic field parallel to the planes. Thus, an enhanced $1/ω$ optical conductivity does not by itself imply enhanced magnetic screening. In view of applications to driven YBCO, where superconducting-like in-plane optics and transient diamagnetism have both been reported, our result provides a symmetry diagnostic: within a phase-synchronization mechanism, the experimentally active low-frequency stiffness modulation must contain a substantial layer-symmetric component.
summary: This theoretical study investigates how periodic driving affects coherence in superconducting bilayers, comparing optical conductivity to magnetic screening. By modeling two types of drive symmetries, the authors find that only layer-symmetric driving enhances both observables simultaneously. This establishes a necessary symmetry condition for interpreting experimental reports of enhanced superconducting behavior.
main_problem: The study aims to theoretically distinguish between enhanced superconducting-like optical conductivity and enhanced magnetic screening in phase-disordered superconducting bilayers subjected to periodic driving.
main_result: Only a layer-symmetric drive enhances both the optical conductivity and the magnetic screening response, providing a symmetry diagnostic for interpreting experimental measurements in cuprates.
method: The analysis uses a bilayer XY model Hamiltonian and simulates dynamics using overdamped Langevin equations to calculate phase correlators and linear response functions.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting bilayer, modeled by phase variables $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$, coupled by Josephson interactions. The dynamics are driven by modulating the in-plane superfluid stiffness in two distinct, symmetric, or antisymmetric ways.
key_observables: Layer-averaged phase correlator ($G_+$) for optical conductivity, and the relative-phase correlator ($G_-$) related to magnetic screening/counterflow.
important_parameters: Drive symmetry (symmetric vs. antisymmetric), temperature relative to $T_c$, and the strength of the applied magnetic field/vector potential.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is above the equilibrium transition temperature ($T > T_c$) and neglects amplitude fluctuations of the superconducting order parameter.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that symmetric driving enhances both $G_+$ and $G_-$, while antisymmetric driving enhances $G_+$ but leaves $G_-$ largely unaffected, confirming the diagnostic.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using the bilayer XY model, analyzes the response to layer-symmetric versus layer-antisymmetric drives by calculating both optical conductivity and magnetic screening kernels, and concludes by interpreting the symmetry dependence of the two observables.
why_interesting: The work provides a crucial symmetry diagnostic tool for interpreting complex, out-of-equilibrium measurements in high-temperature superconductors, linking optical response to underlying magnetic coherence.

For a layer-antisymmetric drive [panel (b)], one plane stiffens while the other softens, so that average-phase correlations can still be enhanced, whereas relative-phase correlations are not.
